summary: Plan is structurally sound as a Q05 fork but 'vol to turnover swap' is not trivial. One HIGH issue (turnover_mat construction requires jp_prices_raw, not jp_returns), two sign-flip items that are easy to miss in copy-paste, and a distributional concern with turnover skewness.

vol_to_turnover_replacement_sufficient.detail: Plan describes turnover_mat as '事前計算、20日ローリングmean' but does not acknowledge that the data source differs from vol_mat. vol_mat is built from jp_returns (already a date x code matrix) via jp_returns.rolling(20).std()*sqrt(252). Turnover requires volume data from jp_prices_raw (a long-format DataFrame with 'code','date','volume' columns). Construction requires: (1) pivot jp_prices_raw volume to wide-format date x code, (2) compute rolling 20-day mean, (3) divide current volume by rolling mean to get relative turnover. This is ~10 extra lines and a different data pipeline, NOT a simple variable name swap.
vol_to_turnover_replacement_sufficient.recommendation: Add explicit turnover_mat construction step in implementation_order between steps 1 and 2. Example: volume_wide = jp_prices_raw.pivot_table(index='date', columns='code', values='volume'); rolling_avg = volume_wide.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean(); turnover_mat = volume_wide / rolling_avg

pass_criteria_direction.detail: Plan correctly states pseudo-DiD < 0 for turnover (high-turnover group has worse post-shock CAR). Q05 uses > 0 for vol (high-vol group rebounds more). Direction logic is correct. However, the bootstrap p-value calculation must also be flipped: Q05 uses np.mean(bs_dids >= pseudo_did_shock) for upper-tail test. Q09 needs np.mean(bs_dids <= pseudo_did_shock) for lower-tail test. This is not mentioned in the plan and is a common copy-paste bug.
pass_criteria_direction.recommendation: Explicitly note in implementation_order: 'flip p-value inequality from >= to <= in bootstrap DiD test, and from > to < in primary_pass check'

spearman_correlation_sign.detail: Plan correctly states Spearman correlation should be negative (bigger shock -> deeper continued decline for turnover-high group). Q05 checks rho > 0.05. Q09 must check rho < -0.05. Plan wording is correct; just needs careful implementation.

turnover_distribution_issues.detail: Turnover ratio (latest_volume / 20d_avg_volume) is right-skewed with heavy tail. On shock days, turnover can spike to 3-10x normal. Median split on such a distribution means: (1) most observations cluster near 1.0 boundary, (2) a few extreme outliers dominate the high-group mean CAR. This differs from vol (annualized rolling std) which is more symmetric and stable. The bootstrap baseline will also be affected since non-shock days have more symmetric turnover.
turnover_distribution_issues.recommendation: Consider log(turnover) for median split, or winsorize at 99th percentile before splitting. At minimum, report the high-group turnover distribution statistics (mean, median, p95, p99) in the output JSON so reviewers can assess sensitivity.

statistical_design.detail: Pseudo-DiD framework with bootstrap baseline is appropriate. K12 reports effect size of -0.6% (much larger than Q05's vol effect of +0.087%), so detection power should be ample even with some distributional noise.

performance.detail: turnover_mat construction adds one pivot + one rolling operation. Bootstrap loop is identical to Q05. No performance concern.

findings_summary.title: Bootstrap p-value inequality must flip from >= to <= for lower-tail test
Turnover right-skew may bias median-split results; consider log-transform or winsorization
Spearman rho sign check must flip from >0.05 to <-0.05

conditions_for_full_approval: Address Finding #1: Plan or code must include explicit turnover_mat construction from jp_prices_raw volume pivot
Address Finding #2: Flip bootstrap p-value inequality direction (>= to <=) and primary_pass check (> 0 to < 0)
Address Finding #4: Flip Spearman rho threshold from positive to negative
optional_improvements: Finding #3: Apply log-transform or 99th-percentile winsorization to turnover before median split
Report turnover distribution statistics (mean, median, p95, p99) in output JSON for downstream review
